---
title: "Research"
---

I want to understand how regulatory DNA determines where transcription starts and
how much of it occurs, and how development and the environment change those
decisions. Most of my work is in plants, and I build the assays, models and
software needed to measure this: genome-wide profiling of transcription initiation
and chromatin, genetics, and sequence-to-function models.

## Transcription initiation and enhancers

Much of what a promoter does is visible only at the level of transcription start
sites. Using csRNA-seq, which captures nascent initiation events directly, I mapped
transcription initiation across the *Arabidopsis* seed-to-seedling transition and
validated divergent transcription genetically. From non-coding transcription I
identified about 1,900 putative enhancers active during germination, and reporter
assays confirmed that transcribed regions of this kind can act as enhancers, showing
that at least some *Arabidopsis* enhancers produce enhancer RNAs, as in animals
([Nature Communications, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46082-5)).

csRNA-seq detects the active enhancers that are transcribed, so it complements
chromatin accessibility rather than replacing it, and I now use the two together to
identify *Arabidopsis* enhancers during development and link them to the genes they
control. With collaborators I am also profiling transcription initiation in the
algal and fungal partners of lichens, building on our work on transposable element
diversification in lichen symbionts
([bioRxiv, 2026](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.14.705750)).

## Transcription in a changing environment

Development is one driver of transcriptional change and the environment is another,
acting over timescales from weeks to minutes. As co-first author I led the
bioinformatics for a multi-laboratory study that followed *Arabidopsis* through
weeks of gradually falling temperatures mimicking autumn and early winter, including
daily fluctuations. We found two distinct transcriptional programmes, one responding
to moderate cooling and one to temperatures below 10 °C, showed that the clock gene
*CCA1* is essential for both, and found that cold-induced genes gain promoter
accessibility while repressed genes keep theirs, so that transcription can resume
quickly when it warms again
([Genome Biology, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-026-04289-3)).

![*Arabidopsis* plants moved from 22 °C into constant, gradually cooling or fluctuating
temperature regimes that follow autumn field temperatures recorded in Sweden. From
Ormancey, Tremblay, Cheng et al. (2026), *Genome Biology*, Fig. 1A–C
([CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)).](images/research/seasons.png){width=65% fig-align="center" fig-alt="Experimental design, temperature profiles and photos of Arabidopsis plants in three temperature regimes"}

## Plant immunity

Immune responses are the fast end of that range. At The Sainsbury Laboratory I study
how plant cells switch them on, combining a csRNA-seq time course with
single-nucleus RNA and ATAC multiomics of *Arabidopsis* seedlings treated with
flg22, a bacterial elicitor of pattern-triggered immunity. The aim is to map the
enhancers that immunity activates, connect them to their target genes and resolve
how each cell type responds. So far the early response and the later cell
type-specific responses share a common signature of WRKY-family motif activity
(posters from [2025](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21476383) and
[2026](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21476601)).

![Single-nucleus multiome profiles of 25,728 nuclei from *Arabidopsis* seedlings,
coloured by cell type. From Tremblay, Pai and Nobori, poster at Plant Biology 2026
([CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)).](images/research/immunity.png){width=50% fig-align="center" fig-alt="UMAP of Arabidopsis seedling nuclei clustered into mesophyll, epidermis, vascular, root and other cell types"}

## Models of regulatory sequence

I train and interpret deep sequence-to-function models of chromatin accessibility
and transcription initiation, and use them to ask which sequence features explain
regulatory activity. At The Sainsbury Laboratory I have trained models from scratch
and fine-tuned ChromBPNet and seq2PRINT on single-cell ATAC-seq data from
flg22-treated *Arabidopsis* seedlings, evaluating their accuracy and biases and
interpreting their predictions with attribution and feature ablation. This builds
on my long-running work on sequence motifs and the
[universalmotif](software.qmd) package.

![A contribution-weight logo of a CACGTG motif, in which bases can contribute
positively or negatively, drawn with universalmotif.](images/research/motif.png){fig-alt="Sequence logo with positive and negative base contributions around a CACGTG motif"}

## Earlier work

For my MSc I studied what happens when plants cannot efficiently recycle
methylthioadenosine (MTA): it builds up in reproductive tissues, disrupts sulfur
assimilation and lowers fertility
([Journal of Experimental Botany, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/erag135)).
Between my MSc and PhD I worked as a bioinformatics research assistant at the
University of Waterloo on the comparative genomics of bacterial pathogens,
including the phylogenomics of 8,839 *Clostridioides difficile* genomes
([PLOS Pathogens, 2020](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1009181)), phylogenetic
profiling of bacterial gene function
([Bioinformatics, 2021](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa1105)), and studies
of *C. difficile* toxin B receptors
([Nature Communications, 2022](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-33964-9)) and
ancient tetanus neurotoxins
([Nature Communications, 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-41174-0)). During
the COVID-19 pandemic I worked with clinicians and virologists on SARS-CoV-2,
predicting its recombination potential
([Journal of General Virology, 2020](https://doi.org/10.1099/jgv.0.001491)) and
profiling viral receptors and interferon responses in human airway epithelium
([European Respiratory Journal, 2020](https://doi.org/10.1183/13993003.01123-2020);
[iScience, 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2021.102477)).
